scope: Abstract sequential typed calls; only described return/state observations; no transport, concurrency, restart or external resources. Lists contain unique task identities and unique creation sequence numbers, boolean match, optional integer priority. Inputs are immutable. No observations beyond this interface are required.

cases.source: Return all matching tasks, once each, as a list. Preserve input. Empty matches return an empty list.
Return all matching tasks, once each, as a list ordered by creation sequence. Preserve input. Empty matches return an empty list.

Filter tasks by requested priority. For tasks with priority, match exactly equal integers. Preserve input and creation order. Return each match once and an empty list for no matches. Tasks may lack priority; their treatment needs a requester decision.
Filter tasks whose priority equals the requested integer. Preserve input and creation order. Return each match once and an empty list for no matches. Treat missing priority as zero.
From a nonempty list with integer priorities return exactly one highest-priority task unchanged. Preserve input. Equal priorities are possible; a required tie policy awaits a requester decision.
From a nonempty list with integer priorities return exactly one highest-priority task unchanged. Preserve input. Choose the earliest creation sequence among ties.

clauses.source_quote: Choose the earliest creation sequence among ties.

cases.source: Return each matching task once, unchanged, preserving input. Empty results are empty lists. Choose ascending or descending priority; equal-priority ties retain creation order on every call. All priorities are integers. Callers must accept either direction.

clauses.source_quote: Choose ascending or descending priority; equal-priority ties retain creation order on every call.

cases.source: Return each matching task once unchanged, preserving input. Empty results are empty lists. Order is unconstrained; callers must not depend on order, including across calls.

clauses.source_quote: Order is unconstrained; callers must not depend on order, including across calls.

cases.source: Given two mathematical integers return their exact sum without state or external effects. An internal loop or direct addition may be used.
Return tasks ordered by creation sequence. Return tasks in reverse creation sequence. Two distinct tasks may be present.
For any integer, return it unchanged if nonnegative; otherwise return ERROR. No effects.
Close takes a state OPEN or CLOSED. On OPEN return OK and set CLOSED; on CLOSED return ERROR unchanged. No other effects.

clauses.source_quote: On OPEN return OK and set CLOSED; on CLOSED return ERROR unchanged.

cases.source: Given a nonempty list of integer-priority tasks return a list drawn from highest-priority tasks in creation order, unchanged. Return all ties once each. Preserve input.
Given ASCII text return lowercase text without effects. Remove leading and trailing ASCII spaces only; preserve internal spaces.

clauses.source_quote: Remove leading and trailing ASCII spaces only; preserve internal spaces.
